Adad-nirari II.fact: Adad-nīrārī II (also spelled Adad-nērārī, which means "Adad (the storm god) is my help") reigned from 911 BCE to 891 BCE. He was the first King of Assyria in the Neo-Assyrian Empire.

Adad-nirari II.question: He was the first King of _____ in the Neo-Assyrian Empire
Adad-nirari II.fact: He was the first King of Assyria in the Neo-Assyrian Empire. He instigated the first renewed period of major expansion following that of the Middle Assyrian Empire which had begun in 1365 BCE under Ashur-uballit I and ended after the death of Ashur-bel-kala in 1053 BCE.

Adad-nirari II.question: He made further gains over _____ under Nabu-shuma-ukin I later in his reign

He made further gains over Babylonia under Nabu-shuma-ukin I later in his reign.

Adad-nirari II.subject: Indian Architecture
Adad-nirari II.question: He also campaigned to the west, subjugating the _____ cities of Kadmuh and Nisibin and their territories
Adad-nirari II.fact: He firmly subjugated the areas previously under only nominal Assyrian vassalage, conquering and deporting troublesome Arameans following a battle at the junction of the Khabur and Euphrates rivers in 910 BC. He also campaigned to the west, subjugating the Aramean cities of Kadmuh and Nisibin and their territories.

Adad-nirari III.fact: Adad-nīrārī III (also Adad-nārārī, meaning "Adad (the storm god) is my help") was the King of Assyria from 811 to 783 BC.

Adad-nirari III.subject: Indian Architecture
Adad-nirari III.question: He was the father of kings Ashur-nirari V, _____ IV, and Ashur-dan III
Adad-nirari III.fact: He was the father of kings Ashur-nirari V, Shalmaneser IV, and Ashur-dan III. According to Adad-nīrārī's inscriptions, he led several military campaigns with the purpose of regaining the strength Assyria enjoyed in the times of his grandfather Shalmaneser III.

Adad-nirari III.subject: Indian Architecture
Adad-nirari III.question: According to Adad-nīrārī's inscriptions, he led several military campaigns with the purpose of regaining the strength _____ enjoyed in the times of his grandfather Shalmaneser III
Adad-nirari III.fact: According to Adad-nīrārī's inscriptions, he led several military campaigns with the purpose of regaining the strength Assyria enjoyed in the times of his grandfather Shalmaneser III. Among his actions was a siege of Damascus in the time of Ben-Hadad III in 796 BC, which led to the eclipse of the Aramaean Kingdom of Damascus and allowed the recovery of Israel under Jehoash (who paid the Assyrian king tribute at this time) and Jeroboam II.

Adad-nirari III.subject: Indian Architecture

Alfred DelBello.fact: In December 1984, DelBello surprised political observers by announcing his resignation from the lieutenant governorship, effective February 1, 1985.
